big_story.headline: $6.3 Billion Stolen from Binance in Largest Crypto Theft on Record
big_story.subhead: IT IS THE LARGEST CRYPTO THEFT ON RECORD, EXCEEDING THE $1.46 BILLION STOLEN FROM THE BYBIT EXCHANGE IN FEBRUARY 2025.
paragraphs: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, said about $6.3 billion in crypto was taken in a security incident on Thursday. Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said an attacker moved roughly $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes. It is the largest crypto theft on record, exceeding the $1.46 billion stolen from the Bybit exchange in February 2025.

In its official statement, Binance said its initial investigation suggests the incident "may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop," which allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions. Binance said it has found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak and will publish a technical post-mortem and an updated Proof of Reserves once the investigation and remediation are complete.

TRM Labs attributed the attack with "high confidence" to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit; Chainalysis also said it has high confidence North Korea was behind it. That is an assessment by private blockchain-intelligence firms and has not been confirmed by law enforcement. The US Secret Service says its investigators are working to identify, freeze, trace and recover the funds.

Binance said about $3 billion of the affected assets has been frozen on-chain with blockchain partners. Freezing is not recovery: issuers such as Tether and Circle can freeze stablecoins remotely, which limits the attacker's ability to cash out but does not by itself return the funds. No issuer can freeze bitcoin or ether that way; for those, tracing and recovery are still possible if the coins move through cooperative exchanges or investigators obtain the keys. Binance says it will cover all losses from its SAFU fund and company funds and that user funds are safe; SAFU held about $1 billion as of February 2026, according to Binance's own FAQ. Withdrawals are temporarily suspended while security checks are completed; deposits continue as normal (Binance statement, updated October 30).

Bitcoin fell about 4-5% over 24 hours to around $77,000 in Friday afternoon New York trading (as of about 1:30 PM ET), after touching a six-week low near $76,300. More than $1.5 billion in leveraged crypto positions was liquidated in 24 hours, mostly long bets (CoinGlass data via CoinDesk). Analysts noted the fall was smaller than the average first-day drop after past exchange hacks, because the breach hit a centralised exchange, not the Bitcoin network itself.

For Indian users: Binance is registered with India's Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-IND) as a reporting entity under anti-money-laundering rules. That registration is a reporting obligation, not a government endorsement or investor protection. Binance says balances are safe, but withdrawals stay paused until its security checks finish.

explains.title: The New Speed of Cyberattacks
paragraphs: The thread connecting October's biggest incidents is stolen credentials plus faster tooling, not one campaign, and not AI everywhere. No AI link has been established in the Binance or Bitget breaches. Chainalysis said proceeds of September's $388 million Bitget theft were being mixed with funds from the Binance breach - a laundering step, not a connection between the two attacks.

Underwater robotics startup Coratia has raised ₹18 crore to support its expansion and technological development. The defense-tech enterprise builds specialized robotic systems tailored for marine exploration and defense sector tasks.

The fresh funding will be utilized to build advanced underwater robots specifically designed for the Indian Navy. This investment underscores rising investor confidence in domestic hardware innovation and defense technology solutions.

story_1.headline: Domestic Coal Production Shields India's Economy
paragraphs: Domestic coal production continues to shield India's economy from severe global price swings as pressure on the energy sector persists. The Coal Secretary highlighted that local output provides a vital buffer against international market volatility.
This domestic insulation helps stabilize industrial input costs across the broader manufacturing and power generation sectors as global commodity markets experience ongoing turbulence.

story_2.headline: Crude Imports Set to Record Highest Ever Levels
paragraphs: India's crude imports are set to record their highest-ever levels at 5.4 to 5.6 million barrels per day in October as refiners actively diversify their supply sources. This strategic shift underscores the country's growing refining capacity and robust domestic fuel demand.
The steady inflow of diversified crude shipments also plays a crucial role in managing national energy security amid shifting geopolitical trade routes and fluctuating global oil benchmarks.

story_3.headline: RBI Reports Significant Credit and Rate Trends
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India has released data showing significant movements in bank credit and interest rate trends for September. These updates offer critical insights into credit growth across various economic sectors as monetary policy developments unfold.

geopolitics.headline: Iran Claims It Seized a US Drone Over the Strait of Hormuz; Washington Says the Report Is False
paragraphs: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Thursday that its electronic-warfare unit detected a US MQM-170 Outlaw drone west of the Strait of Hormuz, took control of its guidance systems and landed it intact on Iranian territory. The IRGC claimed the drone was identifying Iranian air defences along the Gulf coast and had taken off from a southern Gulf state's coast. Iranian state television aired the claim.

US Central Command said the report was false. "In the past weeks and months, the IRGC has repeatedly lied out of desperation, and today is no different," CENTCOM spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins told the Associated Press. The MQM-170 Outlaw, built by Griffon Aerospace, is used by the US military mainly as an aerial target for training and testing, according to The War Zone.

Hours earlier, the IRGC said it destroyed a US MQ-1 drone east of the strait, which it called the 14th such drone it has downed. Iran claims to have destroyed more than 50 US MQ-9 Reaper drones since the war began; DPA notes such claims generally cannot be independently verified, though the US Congressional Research Service says the United States has reported losing or damaging dozens of aircraft and drones since joining Israel's campaign. In 2011, Iran displayed a CIA RQ-170 Sentinel it said it had brought down electronically; the US said that drone malfunctioned.

The US-Israeli war with Iran began on February 28. The Wall Street Journal reported this week that Washington has told Gulf Arab states to prepare for a "short, intense military campaign" against Tehran after the November 3 US midterm elections, though no final decision has been made. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday (Reuters), and President Trump said he believes the war will end soon.

venture_vault.headline: Tensrai Secures ₹3.4 Crore to Automate Existing Industrial Machinery
venture_vault.text: Hyderabad-based physical artificial intelligence startup Tensrai has raised ₹3.4 crore in funding to develop technology that allows legacy industrial machines to operate autonomously. The capital infusion will help the startup scale its automation retrofits, aiding Indian manufacturing units in boosting operational efficiency without capital-intensive hardware replacements.

venture_vault.headline: QwikBuild Raises $2.3 Million Pre-Seed Funding Led by Globalway
venture_vault.text: Proptech startup QwikBuild has secured $2.3 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Japanese firm Globalway. The new capital will support the company's product development and expansion plans in India's rapidly modernizing construction technology ecosystem as demand for digital tools soars.

geopolitics.headline: Oil Nears $118 as Hormuz Tanker Attacks Multiply
geopolitics.text: A tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz was hit on Thursday night by explosives attached to its hull from a small boat, the first successful limpet-mine attack of the war, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said. Iran's IRGC said another tanker struck a mine on Friday on what it called an unauthorised route. Brent futures traded near $117.6-118 a barrel on Friday evening Gulf time (about 9-9:30 PM IST), up roughly 2.5% and the highest since late April, heading for a fourth straight monthly gain of about 13-14%. US WTI traded near $104. Oil exports through the strait fell again last week, shipping data provider Kpler said.
geopolitics.source: Reuters · UK Maritime Trade Operations · Kpler

explains.headline: AI Agents Targeted More Than 2,250 Microsoft 365 Tenants After a ConnectWise Credential Theft
explains.text: October showed how AI tooling is changing the tempo of some major attacks. On October 21, Microsoft reported that a China-state-aligned group it tracks as Storm-0940 used ARTEX, an open-source framework in which AI agents run penetration-test tasks with little human involvement, after a ConnectWise cloud-backup credential was stolen: sign-in attempts against more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants followed, and in several cases the attackers won privileged cloud access within three hours of first targeting an organisation. Security firm Huntress confirmed unauthorised sign-ins at 162 tenants. Microsoft says its own systems were not compromised, and that a sign-in does not by itself prove data was taken.

explains.headline: CERT-In Warns Indian Financial Firms After Payment-API Fund-Transfer Attacks
explains.text: India received its own warning. CERT-In's October 9 advisory, rated critical, says attackers stole payment and partner-bank API credentials at NBFCs, digital lenders, payment firms and wallet operators, then called fund-transfer APIs directly from the victims' own trusted servers, bypassing KYC, sanction and limit checks. The advisory notes the possible use of AI-assisted tools and faster compromise-to-transfer times. The Economic Times reported about 20 institutions were affected. A second CERT-In advisory on October 15 warned of the misuse of open-source agentic AI tools against Indian systems.

explains_rea.headline: REA - separate capability note
explains_rea.text: Separately, October made a phenomenon of REA, short for "Reverse Engineer Anything" - a viral open-source project whose pseudonymous creator, Morluto, spoke to Scientific American this week. REA lets an AI coding agent drive established reverse-engineering tools such as Ghidra, software originally developed by the US National Security Agency, to inspect an app it has no source code for and explain how its features work. That makes software inspection far more accessible: useful for researchers, preservationists and builders studying systems they own, and dual-use in that the same accessibility can serve attackers. There is no evidence linking REA to any of the incidents above.
